newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka's Q1 tea exports up, production falls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka's Q1 tea exports up, production falls.

text.p: Sri Lanka's tea exports for the first quarter this year rose two percent to 59.2 million kg from 58 million kg in the same quarter last year, brokers said on Tuesday.
The figures include tea imported for blending and re-export which amounted to about 2.8 million kg in both years.

Tea export earnings rose 16 percent to 8.6 billion rupees in January-March 1997 from 7.5 billion rupees in the same period in 1996, brokers said. The central bank said on Monday that the Indian Ocean island's tea output in January-March 1997 fell 7.8 percent to 54.6 million kg from 59.2 million kg in the same 1996 period.
Brokers said the crop shortfall was caused by drought over the winter months.
"Rush" crops harvested during the current rainy season could make up for the shortfall, they said.
The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), the world biggest tea market, remained the largest importer of Sri Lankan tea in the first quarter of this year, brokers said.
The CIS bought 13.8 million kg of tea in January-March, up slightly from 13.7 million kg in the same period in 1996. The CIS accounted for 45 percent of all imports of tea in packets.

Last year, the CIS emerged as the biggest importer of Ceylon tea, buying almost 47 million kg, mainly in packets, up from 40 million in 1995. Prices at the Colombo auction, the world's biggest tea auction, shot to record highs last year because of strong demand from the CIS. Turkey was the second biggest buyer of Sri Lankan tea in the first quarter of 1997, importing five million kg, down from 7.2 million kg in the same 1996 quarter. Some of Turkey's imports are re-exported to the southern CIS states. ($1=58.47 rupees)
